---
title: "mean() does not take several numbers the way max() does"
ref: FUN-02
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'mean(1, 5, 3)'
reponse: '1'
attendu: "`3`, the mean of 1, 5 and 3"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
max(1, 5, 3)
sum(1, 5, 3)
mean(1, 5, 3)
median(1, 5, 3)
```
:::

## Why

`max()` and `sum()` gather everything you pass them through `...`. `mean()` and `median()` expect a single vector `x`: the following numbers fill other arguments. In `mean(1, 5, 3)`, `x` is 1, `trim` is 5 and `na.rm` is 3.

The mean of a single value is that value, hence 1. No argument is refused, so no error.

## The remedy

Group the values into a vector with `c()`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
mean(c(1, 5, 3))
median(c(1, 5, 3))
```
:::
